candidates.description: This detector creates spots from a black and white mask. More precisely, all the pixels in the designated channel that have a value strictly larger than 0 are considered as part of the foreground, and used to build connected regions. In 2D, spots are created with the (possibly simplified) contour of the region. In 3D, a spherical spot is created for each region in its center, with a volume equal to the region volume. The spot quality stores the object area or volume in pixels.
candidates.name: Mask detector

candidates.description: This tracker is based on the Linear Assignment Problem mathematical framework. Its implementation is adapted from the following paper: Robust single-particle tracking in live-cell time-lapse sequences - Jaqaman et al., 2008, Nature Methods. Tracking happens in 2 steps: First spots are linked from frame to frame to build track segments. These track segments are investigated in a second step for gap-closing (missing detection), splitting and merging events. Linking costs are proportional to the square distance between source and target spots, which makes this tracker suitable for Brownian motion. Penalties can be set to favor linking between spots that have similar features. Solving the LAP relies on the Jonker-Volgenant solver, and a sparse cost matrix formulation, allowing it to handle very large problems.
candidates.name: LAP Tracker

candidates.name: Detect spots

candidates.description: Splits the incoming data randomly, sending a certain percentage of it to the specified output slot. Negative weights are replaced by zero, and each data item goes to only one slot (no overlaps). This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.
candidates.name: Split data randomly (percentage)

candidates.description: Applies a euclidean distance transform on binary images.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
candidates.name: Euclidean distance transform 2D

candidates.description: Outlines each 3D ROI in the ImageJ 3D suite (IJ3D) as a bounding box, oriented bounding box, convex hull, or surface. Errors can be ignored, in which case affected objects are deleted.
candidates.name: Outline IJ3D ROI

candidates.description: Creates a montage of all input images. Supports 2D and 3D images. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.
candidates.name: Create montage

candidates.description: Applies a mathematical operation between two images with the legacy ImageJ calculator, which runs per 2D slice. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. Old implementation that directly uses the one provided by ImageJ. We recommend to use 'Fast image arithmetics' instead. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Legacy image calculator 2D

candidates.description: Imports a legacy Cellpose model from a saved model file for cell segmentation. It takes one model file as input and produces a legacy Cellpose model that later steps can apply to images.
candidates.name: Import Cellpose model

candidates.description: Filters the input tables, keeping only those that match a condition you write, such as having at least 10 rows or containing a named column. It checks each input table's row count, column count, column names, and annotations, and passes the table through unchanged when the condition is true; otherwise it produces no table.
candidates.name: Filter tables

candidates.description: Filters filament connected components by various properties
candidates.name: Filter filament components

candidates.description: Measures all components in the filament graph. Produces the following measurements: number of vertices number of edges length (sum of edge lengths) skeletonization-corrected length (adding 2 * radius for each vertex with degree 0 and 1 x radius for each vertex with degree 1) confinement ratio (length of the simplified graph divided by the length) number of vertices with specific degrees min/max centroid x/y/z (per vertex) center[min/max][x/y/z] min/max x/y/z (with sphere radius) sphere[min/max][x/y/z] centroid x/y/z/c/t min/max/avg radius/valueYou can learn more about the generated measurements here: https://jipipe.hki-jena.de/documentation/filament-measurements.html
candidates.name: Measure filament components

candidates.description: Merges all incoming 2D slices into a hyperstack. The slice positions within the hyperstack can be controlled via expressions. The node can handle missing and negative slice positions due to a remapping procedure. Please ensure that there are no duplicate locations. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.
candidates.name: Merge 2D slices into hyperstack

candidates.description: Performs fast 2D image arithmetics: it applies a standard arithmetic or logical operation to the pixels of the image, including addition, subtraction, division, multiplication, GAMMA, EXP, LOG, SQR, SQRT, ABS, AND, OR, XOR, minimum, maximum, and more. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Fast image arithmetics 2D

candidates.description: Sets the radius of each filament vertex from the given input image. Please note that if the C/T coordinates are set to zero, the value is extracted from the 0/0 slice. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Set filament vertex radius from image

candidates.description: Performs a Z-Projection. Also supports other axes C-Project/T-Project.
candidates.name: Z-Project

candidates.description: Converts a label image into a set of ROI. Labels must have a value larger than zero to be detected.If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. The Z/C/T coordinates of the source slices are saved inside the ROI.
candidates.name: Labels to ROI

candidates.description: Removes selected text annotations from data items: it takes in data items with text annotations, deletes every annotation matching the configured name or value expression, and outputs the same data items without those annotations.
candidates.name: Remove annotation

candidates.description: Inverts the colors/values p of an image. With 8-bit images, p=255-p. With RGB images, converts each pixel to three 8-bit pixels and uses p=255-p. With 16-bit images, p=65535-p, or p=255-p, p=1024-p, etc. if an "Unsigned 16-bit range" is set using the "Set" option of the Image>Adjust>Brightness/ Contrast dialog. With 32-bit images, p=max-(p-min), where 'min' and 'max' are the minimum and maximum displayed pixel values.
candidates.name: Invert pixel colors/values

candidates.description: Outlines every 2D ROI in the list by converting it to a polygon, hull, box, line, circle or ellipse shape, one operation at a time: Convert to closed polygon Convert to polygon Calculate convex hull Convert to bounding rectangle Convert to minimum bounding rectangle (rotated rectangle) Convert to oriented line Convert to fitted circle Convert to fitted ellipse Apply split fitting to polygons.
candidates.name: Outline 2D ROI (Hull)

candidates.description: Converts 2D ROI into a label image, where each ROI is assigned its own label unless you generate the label value from an expression. If no reference image is provided, the dimensions are estimated from the ROI. The background color (where no ROI is located) is zero. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: 2D ROI to Labels (Expression)

candidates.description: Removes all labels from a label map which touch the edges of the image (in X, Y and Z if the image is 3D). Remaining label elements are renumbered afterwards. Parameters: Image label_map_input, ByRef Image label_map_destination Available for: 2D, 3D Please be aware that this node was generated automatically by JIPipe from existing interfaces provided by CLIJ. Please contact the JIPipe developers if you find any issues.
candidates.name: CLIJ2 Exclude Labels On Edges

candidates.description: Extracts orientation features per pixel from a 2D image, producing the same features as the OrientationJ Analysis.
candidates.name: Orientation features 2D (OrientationJ)

candidates.description: Converts 2D ROI into a label image where each label value comes from mapping the ROI name to a value entry. If no name mapping is provided for a ROI, a unique label is generated. If no reference image is provided, the dimensions are estimated from the ROI. The background color (where no ROI is located) is zero. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: 2D ROI to Labels (by name)

candidates.description: Modifies the tables by executing a Python script per table. Each table is passed as dictionary 'table' with the column name as key and values being an array of strings or doubles. The number of input rows can be accessed via the 'nrow' variable.
candidates.name: Modify tables (Script)

candidates.description: Plots the incoming table(s). This node will create a JFreeChart XY line plot.
candidates.name: JFreeChart XY line plot

candidates.description: Smooths the filaments by downscaling the vertex locations and applying the 'Remove duplicate vertices' operation. The positions are then restored.
candidates.name: Smooth filaments

candidates.description: Adjusts the displayed contrast of the incoming image by re-calibrating its color range in ImageJ, without changing the pixel data. The displayed contrast is stored into the image itself. If you want per-slice contrast, convert to 8-bit or 16-bit with 'Convert image to 8-bit (ImageJ auto-contrast)' or 'Convert image to 16-bit (ImageJ auto-contrast)', or use 'Apply ImageJ auto-contrast per slice' for 32-bit images.
candidates.name: Adjust displayed contrast

candidates.description: Calculates the Morphological Feature Contrast (MFC) of the image. For upper MFC, applies the following transformation to the input image f: MFC+ = MAX(0, f - Opening(r2, Closing(r1, f))). For lower MFC, applies the following transformation to the input image f: MFC- = MAX(0, Closing(r2, Opening(r1, f)) - f). For the full MFC, applies the following transformation to the input image f: MFC = MFC+ + MFC-. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
candidates.name: Morphological Feature Contrast (MFC) 2D

candidates.description: Applies a 3D morphological operation to greyscale images: Erosion, Dilation, Opening, Closing, White Top Hat, Black Top Hat, Gradient, Laplacian, Internal Gradient, or External Gradient. More information (including examples) can be found at https://imagej.net/MorphoLibJ.html If a multi-channel image is provided, the operation is applied to each channel.
candidates.name: Morphological operation 3D

candidates.description: Removes outliers from 2D images by replacing a pixel value with the median of its neighborhood when it deviates too much from it. If a multi-channel image is provided, the operation is applied to each channel. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
candidates.name: Remove outliers 2D

candidates.description: Exports a 3D scene to Collada 1.4.1 (DAE) This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Export 3D scene

candidates.description: Applies a connected components labeling on a mask. Each connected component is assigned a unique value in the output label image. If the image is non-binary, the connected components are generated per-input value. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
candidates.name: Connected components labeling 2D

candidates.description: Converts a labels image into an RGB image for visualization by assigning a color to each label component.
candidates.name: Convert labels to RGB

candidates.description: Converts a 3D mask into a 3D scene mesh by applying the 'Marching cubes' algorithm.
candidates.name: Mask to 3D scene

candidates.description: Produces a sorted results table from an input results table, reordering rows by one or more selected columns. Columns can be matched by name filters, sorted ascending or descending, and strings can use natural order; an optional reverse switch flips the final order.
candidates.name: Sort table rows

candidates.description: Deprecated. Use the node with the same name. Trains a model with Cellpose. You start from an existing model or train from scratch. Incoming images are automatically converted to greyscale. Only 2D or 3D images are supported. For this node to work, you need to annotate a greyscale 16-bit or 8-bit label image column to each raw data input. To do this, you can use the node 'Annotate with data'. By default, JIPipe will ensure that all connected components of this image are assigned a unique component. You can disable this feature via the parameters. This algorithm merges all annotations and data annotations. Use the iteration step settings to determine how annotations and data annotations are merged
candidates.name: Cellpose training (2.x)

candidates.description: Reorders dimensions of hyperstacks. This for example allows you to switch the depth and time axis. If a stack is provided, it is interpreted as hyperstack with depth and with one frame and one channel. 2D images are ignored and passed to the output without processing.
candidates.name: Reorder dimensions

candidates.description: Converts a 2D or 3D ImageJ image into a 32-bit grayscale image, where each pixel or voxel is stored as a 32-bit floating-point value. This is useful when later analysis needs more numeric precision than standard 8-bit or 16-bit images.
candidates.name: Convert image to 32-bit

candidates.description: Takes a 2D or 3D image and converts it to RGB color data, producing an image whose pixels are represented as red, green, and blue channels. This makes the image suitable for steps that expect RGB color input.
candidates.name: Convert image to RGB

candidates.description: Merges 2D ROI lists in a defined order: the ROI from 'Source' are added to the end of the 'Target' list. Compared to 'Merge ROI lists', this node allows to control the order of the operation. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.
candidates.name: Merge 2D ROI lists (ordered)

candidates.description: Sets the properties of every 2D ROI in the list to values computed by user-written expressions. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Set 2D ROI properties from expressions

candidates.description: Adds a new column to the table. By default no changes are applied if the column already exists. Can be optionally configured to replace existing columns.
candidates.name: Add table column

candidates.description: Crops a 2D image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
candidates.name: Crop 2D image

candidates.description: Colors each 3D ROI in the ImageJ 3D suite (IJ3D) by a chosen measurement. It takes 3D ROIs and an optional reference image, measures the selected statistic for each ROI (in physical units when available), maps the values to a color map, and outputs the same 3D ROI list with updated fill colors. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Color IJ3D ROI by statistics

candidates.description: Stores all available information about the vertices into a table. You can learn more about the generated measurements here: https://jipipe.hki-jena.de/documentation/filament-measurements.html
candidates.name: Measure filament vertices

candidates.description: Sets the value/intensity of each filament vertex from the given input image. Please note that if the C/T coordinates are set to zero, the value is extracted from the 0/0 slice. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Set filament vertex value from image

candidates.description: Reslices an image by defining a new Z axis and projecting the image so that this becomes its Z axis, allowing views through other planes.
candidates.name: Reslice

candidates.description: Compares two label or binary images and calculates measurements of their overlap error or agreement. Measurements include: Overlap Jaccard index Dice coefficient Volume Similarity False Negative Error False Positive Error This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Measure label overlap

candidates.description: Applies a mathematical operation with a scalar value to each pixel of a 2D image, using the legacy ImageJ implementation. Supported operations are SET, ADD, SUBTRACT, MULTIPLY, DIVIDE, GAMMA, MINIMUM, MAXIMUM, LOGICAL OR, LOGICAL AND, and LOGICAL XOR. We recommend to use 'Fast image arithmetics' instead.
candidates.name: Legacy image math operation (scalar)

candidates.description: Performs seeded watershed segmentation on a 2D or 3D image, flooding from label markers using flooding simulations on the image. Please note that this node returns labels instead of masks. The markers need to be labels, so apply a connected components labeling if you only have masks. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Seeded watershed

candidates.description: Converts an image into an OME image. Optionally allows the attachment of ROI that are then stored within the OME image This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Image to OME Image

candidates.description: Computes the Gaussian blurred image of an image given two sigma values in X and Y. Thus, the filterkernel can have non-isotropic shape. The implementation is done separable. In case a sigma equals zero, the direction is not blurred. Parameters: Image source, ByRef Image destination, Number sigma_x, Number sigma_y Available for: 2D Please be aware that this node was generated automatically by JIPipe from existing interfaces provided by CLIJ. Please contact the JIPipe developers if you find any issues.
candidates.name: CLIJ2 Gaussian Blur 2D

candidates.description: Deprecated. Please use the new node. Exports incoming images into a non-JIPipe format (PNG, JPEG, BMP, AVI, TIFF). Please note support for input images depending on the file format: PNG, JPEG, BMP: 2D images only AVI: 2D or 3D images only TIFF: All images supported This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Export image

candidates.description: Deprecated. Please use the new node. Exports a results table to CSV/XLSX This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Export table

candidates.description: Evaluates an expression per label: given a table with two numeric columns containing a key and a value, it summarizes all values assigned to a key into a single value. Allows the generation of normalized and cumulative histograms.
candidates.name: Apply expression per label

candidates.description: Runs a custom ImageJ macro. JIPipe will iterate through the iteration steps and execute operations to convert JIPipe data into their ImageJ equivalent (see JIPipe to ImageJ parameter). Then the macro code is executed, followed by operations to import the result data into JIPipe data (see ImageJ to JIPipe parameter). Please feel free to click the 'Load example' button in the parameters to get started. Please keep in mind the following remarks: Input images are opened as windows named according to the input slot. You have to select windows with the select() function or comparable functions. Output images are extracted by finding a window that is named according to the output slot. Ensure to rename() windows accordingly. To extract the 'Results' table output, add an output of type 'Results table' and set the name to 'Results'. Alternatively, you can configure the output in 'JIPipe to ImageJ' and override the name to 'Results' To import other tables, use a different slot name or set the appropriate configuration. Please note that there is only one ROI manager. This is a restriction of ImageJ. Annotations can also be accessed via a function getJIPipeAnnotation(key), which returns the string value of the annotation or an empty string if no value was set. You can define variables that are passed from JIPipe to ImageJ. Variables are also created for incoming path-like data, named according to the slot name. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Run ImageJ Macro

candidates.description: For all linear filament vertex components (all vertices have a degree less than 3), finds the order of each vertex in that line. Also can calculate the distance (in pixels) traveled from the start to the end point. The result is stored in each vertex' metadata field.
candidates.name: Find linear filament vertex order/distance

candidates.description: Produces an 8-bit grayscale ImageJ image by converting the input 2D or 3D ImageJ image to 8-bit, with intensity values from 0 to 255.
candidates.name: Convert image to 8-bit

candidates.description: Generates a pixel value histogram of the input image. It generates following output columns: value, count.
candidates.name: Image to pixel value/count histogram

candidates.description: Draws a scale bar onto the image (via an overlay ROI)
candidates.name: Draw scale bar

candidates.description: Splits high-dimensional image stacks into 2D planes
candidates.name: Split stack into 2D

candidates.description: Extracts statistics for all labels in the image. Statistics are extracted over an image (optional). If no image is supplied, the label itself will be used as the image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Extract label statistics 2D

candidates.description: Combines the 2D ROIs of a list with a logical calculator operation (AND, OR, XOR and related), applied to the whole list at once. The logical operations are applied to the whole list, meaning that an AND operation will create the union of all ROI in the list. If you want to apply the operation only to a sub-set of ROI, preprocess using a ROI splitter algorithm.
candidates.name: 2D ROI calculator (AND/OR/XOR)

candidates.description: Extracts the part of the incoming image inside each 2D ROI by cropping its bounding area. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Extract from 2D ROI

candidates.description: Filters 2D ROI lists, passing on only those lists that match the filter criteria.
candidates.name: Filter 2D ROI list

candidates.description: Splits 2D ROI that consist of multiple sub-ROI into their individual ROI. Such multi-component ROI are for example generated by the ROI calculator.
candidates.name: Split multi-component 2D ROI

candidates.description: Applies a local auto-thresholding algorithm. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. Bernsen recommends a radius of 15 and a contrast threshold of 15. This node requires 8-bit images. Use the corresponding 16-bit node for images with a higher bit depth.
candidates.name: Local auto threshold 2D (Bernsen, 8-bit)

candidates.description: Converts 3D ROI lists into a label image in the ImageJ 3D suite (IJ3D). Depending on the number of objects, an 8-bit, 16-bit, or 32-bit label image is generated. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: IJ3D ROI to labels

candidates.description: Splits the 3D ROI lists in the ImageJ 3D suite (IJ3D) into individual 3D ROI lists, one per ROI.
candidates.name: Split into individual IJ3D ROI lists

candidates.description: Merges multiple parameter sets. To always multiply all incoming parameters, set the iteration step grouping method to 'Multiply'. Parameters with the same unique key are overwritten according to the input slot order. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Merge parameters

candidates.description: Plots the incoming table(s). This node will create a JFreeChart 2D pie plot.
candidates.name: JFreeChart 2D pie plot

candidates.description: Splits a table into multiple tables according to list of selected columns. Sub-tables that have the same values in the selected columns are put into the same output table.
candidates.name: Split table by columns

candidates.description: Trains a segmentation model with Cellpose 3. Cellpose 3 uses a U-Net-based architecture that typically requires more epochs (500 by default) to converge. Incoming images are automatically converted to greyscale. Only 2D or 3D images are supported. For this node to work, you need to annotate a greyscale 16-bit or 8-bit label image column to each raw data input. To do this, you can use the node 'Annotate with data'. By default, JIPipe will ensure that all connected components of this image are assigned a unique component. You can disable this feature via the parameters. Does not support the training of image restoration models. This algorithm merges all annotations and data annotations. Use the iteration step settings to determine how annotations and data annotations are merged
candidates.name: Cellpose segmentation training (3.x)

candidates.description: Trains a segmentation model with Cellpose 2. Cellpose 2 uses a U-Net-based architecture that typically requires more epochs (500 by default) to converge. Incoming images are automatically converted to greyscale. Only 2D or 3D images are supported. For this node to work, you need to annotate a greyscale 16-bit or 8-bit label image column to each raw data input. To do this, you can use the node 'Annotate with data'. By default, JIPipe will ensure that all connected components of this image are assigned a unique component. You can disable this feature via the parameters. This algorithm merges all annotations and data annotations. Use the iteration step settings to determine how annotations and data annotations are merged
candidates.name: Cellpose segmentation training (2.x)

candidates.description: Converts the filaments to an RGB image by rendering them onto it. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Convert filaments to RGB

candidates.description: Extracts statistics of the whole image or a masked part. Please note that this node will not be able to extract the shape of masked areas. All shape-description features (Centroid, Perimeter, ...) are calculated on the rectangle formed by the image dimensions. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Extract image statistics

candidates.description: Extracts statistics of the whole image or a masked part. The table columns are created via expressions. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Extract image statistics (Expression)

candidates.description: Gets the pixels of an image as a table by extracting every pixel value with its coordinates. The table always includes columns x, y, z, c, and t. For greyscale images, the value is stored into a column value. For color images, column names depend on the color space.
candidates.name: Get pixels as table

candidates.description: Performs a Z-projection, classic flavor, with a wrapper around the native ImageJ function that can only handle 3D images. If you have a hyperstack (4D+), use the other Z-project algorithm.
candidates.name: Z-Project (classic)

candidates.description: Extracts the OME metadata from an OME image and outputs it as OME-XML data. It takes an OME image and produces the XML that describes its channels, sizes, and acquisition metadata.
candidates.name: Extract OME XML

candidates.description: Finds the local maxima of each image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
candidates.name: Local maxima 2D

candidates.description: Applies the vesselness filter developed by Frangi et al.
candidates.name: Frangi vesselness

candidates.description: A ridge detector that detects lines and outputs a binary mask where lines are detected.
candidates.name: Ridge detector

candidates.description: Makes the input image have the same dimensions as the maximum of all images. You can choose to make them equal in width/height, and hyperstack dimensions (Z, C, T). Optionally annotates each output with information about its original size. This node allows multiple inputs and outputs (IO-configuration). The maximum is calculated over all inputs and then returned via the corresponding output. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.
candidates.name: Equalize hyperstack dimensions (maximum)

candidates.description: Scales a 2D image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
candidates.name: Scale 2D image

candidates.description: Imports one or a selection of pretrained Cellpose 3.x image restoration models
candidates.name: Pretrained Cellpose 3.x image restoration model

candidates.description: Applies an expression to the whole table. Each entry in the list of processors generates a column.
candidates.name: Apply expression to table (columns)

candidates.description: Extracts a value from the input text data (via XPath) and annotates the data with the result. Please visit https://www.w3schools.com/xml/xpath_intro.asp to learn about XPath.
candidates.name: Annotate with XML values

candidates.description: Prettify XML data into a formatted, more readable version, using a configurable indentation level and optionally omitting the XML declaration.
candidates.name: Prettify XML

candidates.description: Runs Cellpose restoration on the input image with the given model(s). Cellpose provides algorithms for denoising (similar to noise2void), deblurring, and upsampling. This node supports operations in 3D and executing Cellpose for each 2D image plane. Please note that you need to setup a valid Python environment with Cellpose installed. This algorithm merges all annotations and data annotations. Use the iteration step settings to determine how annotations and data annotations are merged
candidates.name: Cellpose image restoration (3.x)

candidates.description: Extracts the data stored in a chosen data annotation and makes it the main output. It takes a data item with named annotations, selects the annotation matching the configured name, and outputs that annotation's data as a new data item; missing annotations can be ignored or raise an error.
candidates.name: Extract data annotations

candidates.description: Merges greyscale image planes into one multi-channel image with the classic ImageJ channel merging algorithm, which creates either an RGB or a composite image. We recommend to use Blend images for creating renders and Merge channels (composite) that provide more options for the specific use cases. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Merge channels (classic)

candidates.description: Enhances local contrast in each region of the image by applying 'Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization' (CLAHE). Composite color images are converted into their luminance. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the results are generated for each 2D slice.
candidates.name: Enhance local contrast (CLAHE)

candidates.description: Filters the ROI list elements via statistics. Statistics are extracted over an image (optional). If no image is supplied, the label itself will be used as the image. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: Filter labels by statistics 2D

candidates.description: Gets the label boundaries: it creates a mask that is 255 at the boundary between two labels and background.
candidates.name: Get label boundaries

candidates.description: It takes an ImageJ image and produces a copy with the overlay removed, so any 2D ROI or 3D ROI markings are no longer displayed.
candidates.name: Remove overlay

candidates.description: Thresholds the 8-bit 2D image with a manually set threshold range. If higher-dimensional data is provided, the filter is applied to each 2D slice.
candidates.name: Manual threshold 2D (8-bit)

candidates.description: Manually thresholds color (RGB) images: a user-defined min/max threshold is applied to each color channel, producing a binary mask.
candidates.name: Manual color threshold (RGB)

candidates.description: Performs 3D watershed segmentation with the ImageJ 3D suite (IJ3D). It works with two images: one with the seeds of the objects (from local maxima, see 3D filters), the other with signal data. A first threshold selects the seeds (value > threshold1), a second clusters voxels (value > threshold2). Voxels are assigned to seeds in descending order of voxel value. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of one data item per slot.
candidates.name: IJ3D Watershed 3D segmentation

candidates.description: Creates iteration steps from the incoming data and merges them into data table data. Such tables might be needed for some nodes that process lists of data. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.

candidates.description: Template matching is an algorithm that can be used for object-detections in grayscale images. To perform template matching you will need a template image that is searched in the target image. The best is to simply crop a typical region of interest from a representative image. The algorithm computes the probability to find one (or several) template images provided by the user into a larger image. The algorithm uses the template image as a sliding window translated over the image, and at each position of the template computes a similarity score between the template and the image patch. This results in a correlation map, for which the pixel value at position (x,y) is proportional to the similarity between the template and image patch, at this (x,y) position in the image. The computation of the correlation map is followed by extrema detection to list the possible locations of the template in the image. Each extrema corresponds to the possible location of a bounding box of dimensions identical to the template. The extrema detection can list a large number of extrema in the first place. Usually a threshold on the score is then used to limit this number (i.e. returning local extrema with a score above/below the threshold). To prevent overlapping detection of the same object, Non-Maxima Supression is performed after extrema detection. Please visit https://github.com/multi-template-matching/MultiTemplateMatching-Fiji/wiki for more information about the Multi-Template Matching plugin. This algorithm groups the incoming data based on the annotations. Those groups can consist of multiple data items. If you want to group all data into one output, set the matching strategy to 'Custom' and leave 'Data set matching annotations' empty.
candidates.name: Multi-Template matching
